thread.title: Fed says it turned over $80.2 billion to Treasury last year - MarketWatch

author: Greg Robb
title: Fed says it turned over $80.2 billion to Treasury last year - MarketWatch
text:
Getty Images The Federal Reserve Building is seen from the air over Washington, DC, The Federal Reserve said Wednesday it transferred $80.2 billion in earnings to the U.S. Treasury during 2017, as it continued to rake in huge profits from the interest income on the securities it owns.
Even so, the remittance is down from $91.5 billion in 2016, the Fed said. The drop in earnings came as the Fed had to pay more interest to banks for reserves parked at the central bank. The Fed paid $26 billion in interest this year, the Fed said in a statement.
The Fed’s profits dwarf others in the private sector. Apple AAPL, -0.40% , for instance, earned $48.35 billion in the 12 months ending Sept. 30.
The central bank’s profits limit the red ink from federal spending. The budget deficit, which includes the Fed profits, was $666 billion in the Sept-ending fiscal year .
The large transfers are a side benefit from the Fed’s controversial bond-buying program that has resulted in the central bank amassing a $4.5 trillion balance sheet. The Fed earned nearly $114 billion in interest income in 2017, as well as $1.9 billion in foreign currency gains.
The central bank’s remittances are expected to dwindle as the Fed raises interest rates. Analysts said there is a risk the Fed could suffer losses on its holdings if interest rates rise sharply.
Last September, the Fed launched a program to gradually shrink its balance sheet.
In a new research paper released this week, Fed economists argued that this the slow shrinking of the balance sheet reduces the likelihood of any losses.
Fed Chairwoman Janet Yellen and her predecessor Ben Bernanke have always argued that any losses would be small compared with the income transferred to Treasury over the life of the program.
